riddle: Snowy white and silent-winged, I carried letters for the Boy Who Lived. Hagrid bought me for the boy's eleventh birthday, and my name came out of a history book. What is my name?
Scarlet and steaming, I leave London every first of September from a platform most travellers walk straight past. A witch pushes a sweet trolley down my corridors. What am I?
Say my name and your opponent's wand flies out of their grip. The Boy Who Lived used me so often it became his signature move, right up to his final duel. What spell am I?
Old, patched and frayed, I sit on a stool once a year and peer into eleven-year-old minds to decide where each one belongs. A sword once came out of me. What am I?
hint: Worn on the first night of term.

riddle: No bigger than a walnut, golden, with fluttering silver wings, I dart around the pitch dodging grasping hands. Catch me and your team gets 150 points. What am I?
Silvery, water-like fabric that reached a first-year as a Christmas present, once his father's. Throw me over your shoulders and you vanish from sight. What am I?
hint: Great for sneaking to the library at night.

riddle: I look like a blank old parchment until you tap me and swear a mischievous oath. Then I show every corridor of Hogwarts and a labelled dot for every person inside. Four school friends made me. What am I?
A house-elf with eyes like tennis balls, I stole a boy's letters and sealed his train barrier to keep him away from school. A sock hidden in a book finally set me free. Who am I?
Half-giant, bushy-bearded and fond of dangerous pets, I delivered a baby on a flying motorbike and years later broke into a hut on a sea rock to tell him he was a wizard. Who am I?
Rearrange the letters of my birth name and you get my grand new title. Most wizards are too scared to say it, so they use vague phrases instead. I split my soul to cheat death. Who am I?
A headmaster with a long silver beard and half-moon spectacles, I love sherbet lemons and keep a phoenix in my office. My surname is an old word for bumblebee. Who am I?
hint: Head of Hogwarts for most of the series.

riddle: The brightest witch of her year, daughter of two dentists, my hand is always up in class and I once hit a smug blond boy in the face. Who am I?
hint: One third of the famous trio.

riddle: Youngest son of a big red-headed family, I am terrified of spiders, started school with my older brother's used wand and a rat in my pocket. Who am I?
Seven players a side, three kinds of ball, six tall hoops, and everyone is on a broomstick. Wizards go wild for my World Cup. What sport am I?
hint: Muggles now play a version without flying.

riddle: My founder prized courage and daring. My colours are scarlet and gold, my animal is a lion, and my common room hides behind a portrait of a large lady in pink. Which house am I?
Ambitious and cunning, my students sleep in dungeon dormitories beneath the lake. My colours are green and silver and my emblem is a serpent. Which house am I?
Loyal, patient and hard-working, I welcome anyone willing to work. My emblem is a badger, my colours are yellow and black, and a jolly friar is my house ghost. Which house am I?
Wit and learning are my treasure. My common room door has no password, only a question asked by an eagle-shaped knocker. Blue is my colour. Which house am I?

A first-year charm that makes a feather float. Swish and flick, and pronounce it properly or nothing rises. A troll was knocked out when its own club dropped on its head thanks to me. What spell am I?
hint: Hermione got it right first time.

riddle: Whisper me and the tip of your wand glows like a tiny torch. My opposite snuffs the light back out. What spell am I?
I am not the words you shout but the silvery animal that bursts from your wand when you focus on a happy memory. Dementors flee from me. What am I?
hint: Harry's takes the shape of a stag.

riddle: Tall, hooded and scabby-handed, I glide around a wizard prison and drain every happy feeling nearby. The worst thing I can give you is a kiss. What am I?
Half horse, half eagle, I demand a respectful bow before you come near. I lashed out at a rude student, was condemned, and escaped with help from a turned hourglass. What is my name?
Three heads, one sweet name. I guarded a trapdoor in a forbidden third-floor corridor and fell asleep whenever someone played me music. Who am I?
I arrive as a red envelope. Ignore me and it gets worse; open me and I yell my sender's anger at full volume for the whole hall, then burst into flames. What am I?
A tiny hourglass on a long chain. Spin me and you slip back a few hours, enough to attend two classes at once or save a hippogriff. What am I?
hint: How Hermione took so many subjects.

riddle: Blood-red and hidden inside a mirror at the end of a school year, I turn metal into gold and make an elixir that keeps you alive for centuries. What am I?
Stand before me and you see not your reflection but your heart's deepest desire. Read my name backwards to understand me. What am I?
hint: Harry saw his family in it.

riddle: I am an ordinary-looking object holding a torn-off piece of a dark wizard's soul. Every one of me must be destroyed before he can die. What am I?
hint: The diary was the first to be destroyed.

riddle: Tap the right brick in a yard behind a London pub and I open up: a crooked cobbled street of wand shops, cauldrons, owls and a goblin bank. Where am I?
White marble, bronze doors and goblins behind every counter. My vaults lie deep under London, reached by wild rattling carts, and a dragon guarded some of the oldest. What am I?
hint: Where the Potters kept their gold.

riddle: A fortress on a lonely island far out at sea, guarded for years by soul-draining creatures. A black-haired prisoner famously broke out of me by slipping past as a dog. What am I?
I cannot do magic and usually have no idea it exists. The Dursleys are proud to be me. What do British wizards call me?
hint: Most of the people reading this are one.

riddle: A plant with a baby-faced root. Pull me up without earmuffs and my scream can knock you out, yet my juice cured the students who were turned to stone. What am I?
Muddy, bubbling and foul-tasting, I let you look like someone else for an hour, but only after you add a bit of them. A cat hair once gave a clever girl whiskers. What am I?
Sweets that are a real gamble: you might get strawberry, or earwax, dirt or liver. An old headmaster once got an unlucky one. What are they?
hint: Every flavour, and they mean it.

riddle: The moment my box opens I try to leap away. Inside you also get a card of a famous witch or wizard, which many people collect. What sweet am I?
hint: You might be hunting one right now.

riddle: Planted on the school grounds to hide the entrance to a secret tunnel, I thrash my branches at anyone who gets close. Two boys once crashed a flying car into me. What am I?
A blue Muggle car enchanted to fly and turn invisible, I carried two boys to school after they missed the train, then ran wild in the Forbidden Forest. What am I?
Gryffindor's ghost, a botched beheading left my head attached by a sliver of skin, so I am never allowed to join the proper Headless Hunt. Who am I?
hint: He can tip his head off like a lid.

riddle: A gloomy ghost who haunts a girls' toilet at Hogwarts, I sulk, wail, flood the floor and dive into the plumbing when upset. Who am I?
Scarlet and gold, I burst into flames when old and am reborn from my ashes. My tears heal, I live in the headmaster's office, and my tail feathers sit inside two famous wands. Who am I?
A huge snake who never leaves her master's side. I held a piece of his soul, and a brave boy with a sword finally ended me. Who am I?
A tired old rat missing a toe, handed down to the youngest Weasley boy. For twelve years nobody knew I was really a man in hiding. Who am I?
Wild-haired and fanatically loyal to the Dark Lord, I spent years in Azkaban. I am cousin to Sirius Black and aunt to Tonks. Who am I?
Pale, pointy-faced and smug, I sneered at the Boy Who Lived for years; in the books we first met at a robe fitting. My father sat on the school's board of governors. Who am I?
I love pink cardigans, plates of kittens and rules. As a Defence teacher I made students write lines with a quill that cut the words into their own hands. Who am I?
hint: She took over Hogwarts for a while.

riddle: Strict Transfiguration professor and head of Gryffindor, I can turn into a tabby cat with square markings around my eyes. Who am I?
Harry's godfather, I was wrongly blamed for betraying my best friends and escaped a wizard prison in the shape of a big shaggy black dog. Who am I?
Point your wand at a locked door, say my word, and the lock clicks open. A clever first-year used me to escape into a forbidden corridor. What spell am I?
Say my single word with an object's name and it zooms straight into your hand. Harry used me to fetch his broom while facing a dragon. What spell am I?
Aim me at a shape-shifter that has taken the form of your worst fear and picture it looking silly. Laughter defeats it. What spell am I?
A giant serpent hidden under the school. Meet my eyes directly and you die; see them only in a reflection and you are left stiff as stone. A rooster's crow is deadly to me. What am I?
I appear on the seventh floor only when you walk past three times needing me, and I become whatever you need: a training hall, a hiding place or a mountain of junk. What am I?
Served foaming in tankards in Hogsmeade, I warm you up on a snowy day and can leave a creamy moustache. What drink am I?
Raised by a stern grandmother, I kept losing my toad on the train, shone at Herbology, and in the final battle beheaded a great snake with a sword pulled from a hat. Who am I?
I am no ghost but a mischief-making spirit who belongs to the castle. I drop water balloons, sing rude rhymes and am scared of only one house ghost. I was cut from the films. Who am I?
The Weasley family's ancient, ragged grey owl. I brought the Howler that screamed at Ron over breakfast in the Great Hall, and crash-landed on the table doing it. Who am I?
hint: The Weasleys really need a new owl.

riddle: Ginger, bandy-legged and flat-faced, in the books I leapt onto a boy's head in a pet shop and went home with a bushy-haired witch. I spent a whole year hunting her friend's pet rat, and I was right to. Who am I?
A shallow stone basin filled with swirling silver. Draw a thought from your temple with a wand, drop it in, and you can dive inside the memory. What am I?
hint: It lives in the headmaster's office.

riddle: A potion that shines like molten gold. A small sip makes everything go your way for a while. A boy won a tiny bottle of me in his first lesson with a new Potions master. What am I?
Carved with a Thestral-hair core, I pass to whoever defeats my last master. I am said to be unbeatable and am one of the three Deathly Hallows. What am I?
I look like a silver cigarette lighter, but click me and every nearby light is sucked inside. Left to a red-haired boy in a will, I later guided him back to his friends. What am I?
hint: Dumbledore used it on Privet Drive.

riddle: A narrow, dusty shop in London, boxes piled to the ceiling. My sign claims we have made our product since 382 BC, and the item picks its owner, not the other way round. What shop am I?
hint: Every first-year's first stop for magic.

riddle: A loud, bright joke shop in Diagon Alley run by red-haired twins, stocked with Skiving Snackboxes, fake wands and daydream charms. What shop am I?
hint: Their exit from school was legendary.

riddle: The finest sweet shop in Hogsmeade, stuffed with fizzing sherbet and sugar quills. A secret passage from the school ends in my cellar. What am I?
Villagers call me the spookiest building in Britain, but the howls came from a young werewolf hidden inside every full moon. A tunnel under a violent tree leads to me. What am I?
I am London's wizarding hospital, hidden behind a shabby closed-down department store. A former teacher who wiped his own memory lives on one of my long-term wards. What am I?
Number twelve on my London square hides between eleven and thirteen. Home of an old pure-blood family, I served as secret headquarters for a resistance group. Where am I?
A village where a dark curse rebounded one Halloween night. In the book, the war memorial in my square turns into a statue of a family of three whenever a witch or wizard walks past. Where am I?
A seaside home near Tinworth where a curse-breaker lives with his part-Veela wife. A brave house-elf lies buried in my garden. What am I?
A French school whose students arrived in a huge powder-blue carriage pulled by giant winged horses. Our headmistress stands roughly as tall as Hagrid. What school am I?
A northern school rumoured to teach the Dark Arts. My students arrived by a ship that rose out of the lake, led by a famous international Seeker. What school am I?
A red leather ball about the size of a football. Chasers pass me between them and throw me through hoops for ten points. What am I?
A heavy black iron ball that rockets around trying to knock players off their brooms. One was tampered with to chase a single boy and broke his arm. What am I?
In Quidditch I hover in front of three tall hoops and try to stop the red ball getting through. Oliver Wood played me for Gryffindor. What position am I?
In Quidditch I carry a short club and whack iron balls away from my teammates and towards the other side. Red-haired twins played me for Gryffindor. What position am I?
The fastest racing broom of its day, zero to 150 miles an hour in ten seconds. One arrived for Christmas with no note and was taken apart to check for jinxes. What am I?
Hufflepuff's plump, cheerful, robed ghost, I am always urging the others to give the castle poltergeist one more chance. Who am I?
Ravenclaw's tall, proud ghost. In life I was the founder's own daughter, and I stole her diadem and hid it inside a tree in a forest in Albania. Who am I?
Slytherin's ghost, hollow-eyed and grim, splattered with silvery bloodstains and rattling the chains I wear as penance. Even the castle's troublemaking spirit behaves around me. Who am I?
A small golden cup with two handles and a badger engraved on it. A dark wizard took me from an old collector, and I later sat hidden in a bank vault. What am I?
A muttering old house-elf devoted to a pure-blood family and a screaming portrait. I hid a stolen locket for years and later led the elves into battle. Who am I?
A goblin who once led a first-year down to his vault, I later helped break into the bank in exchange for a sword, then snatched it and ran. Who am I?
hint: He wanted the sword of Gryffindor.

riddle: A palomino centaur cast out by my herd for teaching humans, I took over Divination in a classroom turned into a forest. Who am I?
Skeletal, black and leathery-winged, I pull the school carriages. You can only see me if you have seen someone die. What creature am I?
Hagrid's giant half-brother, a small one at about sixteen feet, I was hidden in the Forbidden Forest and learned to say a version of Hermione's name. Who am I?
A Norwegian Ridgeback hatched in a wooden hut from an egg won off a stranger in a pub. I bit a boy's hand and was secretly sent off to Romania. What is my name?
Swallow this slimy plant and you grow gills and webbed hands for about an hour. It carried a champion through the lake task. What am I?
hint: Dobby brought it in the book.

riddle: Three clear drops of me and you will spill the truth to any question. Snape once threatened to slip me into a student's drink. What am I?
The most powerful love potion, with a mother-of-pearl sheen and steam rising in spirals. It smells different to everyone, of whatever they find attractive. What am I?
A smoking, foul potion that regrows missing bones overnight, painfully. A vain teacher's botched spell left a boy's arm boneless, and I fixed it. What am I?
A shrivelled stone from a goat's stomach that protects against most poisons. A student saved his poisoned friend by shoving me down his throat. What am I?
hint: Ron's birthday could have gone badly.

riddle: A dark spell scribbled in a Potions textbook margin with a note saying it is for enemies. Cast carelessly in a bathroom, it slashed a rival across the chest. What spell am I?
A binding promise sealed with joined hands while fiery bands wrap around them. Break it and you die. Snape made one with Draco's mother. What am I?
Born to wizarding parents but with no magic of my own. The Hogwarts caretaker is one and secretly sent off for a correspondence course to fix it. What am I?
An odd magazine whose editor lives near the Weasleys, famous for stories about strange creatures. It once printed Harry's full interview when no one else would. What am I?
A shady side street beside London's main wizarding shopping street, full of dark objects, poisonous candles and shifty dealers. A boy landed here after a bad trip by Floo. Where am I?
The school nickname of a Marauder who could turn into a stag. His son's Patronus takes the same shape. What was the nickname?
A reporter with jewelled glasses and an acid-green quill that twists every word, I snooped on the Triwizard champions as an unregistered beetle Animagus. Who am I?
A grimy pub on a side street of Britain's only all-wizard village, run by the headmaster's goat-loving brother. A painting upstairs hides a passage into the castle. What am I?
A soot-stained row of mill-town houses by a dirty river, where a Potions master spent his summers. Two sisters visited me in secret at the start of the sixth book. Where am I?
A village where a snobbish Muggle family's big house stands on a hill and a dark wizard's mother grew up in a shack nearby. My graveyard saw a dark rebirth. Where am I?
A tall fortress a dark wizard built to hold his enemies. After his defeat in 1945 he spent the rest of his life locked in its topmost cell. What is it called?
A daring Quidditch move: a Seeker dives as if he has spotted the Snitch, tricking the other Seeker into following him straight into the ground. Krum did it at the World Cup. What is it called?
A tiny, round, gold-feathered bird, incredibly fast, once hunted during Quidditch matches until it almost died out. A winged metal ball was invented to replace me. What am I?
I nodded off by the staffroom fire, got up the next morning to teach and left my body behind. I have droned through History of Magic ever since. Who am I?
hint: The only ghost on the staff.

riddle: A delicate crown said to sharpen the wearer's wisdom, lost for centuries and later hidden among the junk of a secret room. A dark wizard turned me into a soul-container. What am I?
A tearful house-elf dismissed after being found holding a stolen wand at the World Cup, I drowned my sorrows in butterbeer in the Hogwarts kitchens. Who am I?
A small, twig-like creature with bark skin and long fingers. I guard trees good for wand wood and will go for your eyes if disturbed, but woodlice calm me. What am I?
hint: Hagrid taught them in Care of Magical Creatures.

riddle: A small, horned, pale-green water demon with long brittle fingers, I lurk in the school lake. A werewolf teacher kept one of me in a tank for a lesson. What am I?
hint: Break its grip by the fingers.

riddle: Corpses animated by dark magic to obey a master. We swarmed out of a black lake in a sea cave to guard a locket, and fire drives us back. What are we?
hint: Dumbledore used a ring of fire.

riddle: Not the green skull and serpent in the sky, but the word that conjures it. It shot up over the woods after the Quidditch World Cup. What incantation am I?
A spell a teenage half-blood invented and scribbled in a textbook margin. It fills nearby ears with a strange buzzing so nobody can overhear your conversation. What spell am I?
hint: Harry used it in sixth year.

riddle: A silent jinx from a Potions textbook margin that yanks someone upside down by the ankle; a second spell lets them drop. What spell am I?
A charm that hides a secret inside a single living person, called the Secret-Keeper. The Potters trusted theirs to the wrong friend. What charm am I?
hint: Only the Keeper can reveal it.

riddle: A rare witch or wizard born able to change their looks at will, no potion needed. A clumsy Auror with bubblegum-pink hair is one. What is the word for what I am?
Younger brother of a famous escaped prisoner, I joined the Death Eaters, turned on my master, and left a note in a fake locket signed only with my initials. Who am I?
A tiny, reckless knight in a painting who challenges everyone to duels and keeps falling off his fat grey pony. I guarded Gryffindor Tower for a while with absurd passwords. Who am I?
hint: He replaced the Fat Lady briefly.

riddle: The family name of the three brothers from a wizarding fairy tale who were said to receive a wand, a stone and a cloak from Death. What was their surname?
A Quidditch team in bright orange robes that has not won the league in more than a century. The youngest Weasley boy covers his bedroom walls with our posters. Which team am I?

A withered, shrivelled thing that gives light only to whoever holds it. In the books a blond boy begged his father to buy it in a dark shop, and years later used one to lead Death Eaters through a blacked-out castle. What am I?
The house-elf rights society a determined witch founded in fourth year. Her friends read its initials as a word that means being sick, much to her annoyance. What word do the initials spell?

A small grey potted plant covered in boils where a cactus would have spines, a birthday gift to a Herbology lover. Prod it and it squirts foul-smelling Stinksap all over a train compartment. What am I?
To get into the Hogwarts kitchens you tickle one fruit in a big painting of a fruit bowl until it giggles and turns into a door handle. Which fruit is it?
hint: Fred and George know the trick.
